attempts.label: DANDI:000248
attempts.entry_title: Illusory contour responses in mouse visual cortex, Neuropixels (Shin et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the Neuropixels findings of Shin, Ogando, Abdeladim and colleagues (2025) on dandiset 000248, which holds 12 Neuropixels sessions with six probes in V1, LM, RL, AL, PM and AM while mice viewed illusory contour images. It counts the units and the IC-encoders and segment responders, selects exclusively center-responsive V1 units, repeats the analyses on fixed-gaze trials, computes cross-correlograms between V1 and higher visual areas, and decodes the images and the inference of the illusory contour from each area. The 2p imaging and holography data of the paper are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: The Neuropixels sessions hold 150 +/- 20 V1 RS units and 597 +/- 46 higher visual area RS units per session (mean +/- s.e.m., 12 sessions).
outcomes.source: Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: 12 sessions from 12 mice; mean ± s.e.m. = 150 ± 20 V1 RS units and 597 ± 46 higher visual area RS units across sessions
outcomes.notes: V1 holds 150.3 +/- 19.8 RS units per session (1,804 in all) and the five higher visual areas 582.8 +/- 43.3 (mean +/- s.e.m., 12 sessions), within 150 +/- 20 and 597 +/- 46. Dropping the units labelled noise gives 131.4 and 509.9 (variant).

outcomes.statement: Across the ICwcfg0 and ICwcfg1 blocks, 159 of 1,804 V1 RS units are IC-encoders.
outcomes.source: Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Across ICwcfg0 and ICwcfg1, 159 of 1,804 V1 RS units were identified as IC-encoders in the Neuropixels dataset
outcomes.notes: 159 of 1,804 V1 RS units are IC-encoders in at least one of ICwcfg1 and ICwcfg0 (reading a), the paper's number; the sum of the two blocks' counts (reading b) is 163, also within 159 +/- 15.9.

outcomes.statement: The Neuropixels data hold 87 V1 IC-encoders and 636 V1 segment responders (the sets whose layer distribution Extended Data Fig. 6b shows).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 6b legend
outcomes.quote: For the Neuropixels dataset, proportion of V1 IC-encoders (left, n = 87) and V1 segment responders (right, n = 636) in each layer
outcomes.notes: Reading (b1), all V1 units in the files in ICwcfg1, gives 87 IC-encoders and 636 segment responders, the paper's numbers exactly. Dropping the units whose quality label is noise (b2) gives 79 and 566 (566 outside 636 +/- 63.6). Reading (a) gives 79 and 526 (the Fig. 2d counts) and reading (c) 159 and 684; neither puts both counts within tolerance. The layer proportions are shown (IC-encoders 35.6% in layer 2/3, segment responders 28.1%).
deviations: Assumption. Reading (b), "all units not classified as noise", is taken as every unit in the files, because the Methods say "all units not classified as noise were packaged into Neurodata Without Borders" files. The files also carry a quality column with 322 V1 units labelled noise; dropping them (b2) does not reproduce the segment responder count. The exact match of both counts under (b1) supports the assumption. Asked of the authors under findings (methods_unavailable).

outcomes.statement: IC-encoders are found in every visual area, in the Neuropixels and in the calcium imaging data.
outcomes.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6c and 6d legends
outcomes.quote: Using the same approach as above for V1, we could identify IC-encoders throughout these visual areas both in the electrophysiology and in the calcium imaging datasets
outcomes.notes: Neuropixels part. All six areas hold IC-encoders in ICwcfg1: 79 (V1), 48 (LM), 73 (RL), 64 (AL), 59 (PM) and 49 (AM), in 8 to 12 sessions per area, 3.4% to 5.0% of RS units on average. The calcium imaging part of the statement is not in the dandiset and is not tested.

outcomes.statement: In the Neuropixels data, 18 of 1,804 V1 RS units respond exclusively to the grating patch at the center position (the illusory gap region) of the receptive field mapping block.
outcomes.source: Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1e legend
outcomes.quote: In the Neuropixels data, there were n = 18 exclusively center-responsive neurons of 1,804 V1 RS units
outcomes.notes: The V1 RS count is 1,804, as in the paper, but 44 units are exclusively center-responsive under reading (a) and 52 under reading (b), against 18 +/- 1.8. Before the exclusivity rule, 474 units have the center as best position; under (a), 383 of them have at least one position passing the code's Holm step, 68 have exactly one position passing, and for 44 that position is the center; under (b), 602 units have the center passing Holm with a mean above the spontaneous windows and 52 of them have no other position passing. Units in both readings 5; reading (a) without the units labelled noise 37. The analyzeRFCI.m code could not be compared line by line in this run, so a difference in the selection procedure is possible.

outcomes.statement: Of the exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, 66.7% respond substantially to the IC image and 77.8% to the real-edge (IRE) image of their preferred IRE orientation, although the IC image has no contrast in their receptive field.
outcomes.source: Figure 1f legend; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Bottom, individual neurons with substantially I C -responsive (left; 66.7%) and I RE -responsive (right; 77.8%) neurons marked in magenta on the y axis
outcomes.notes: No combination of fig1e reading, test and block puts both fractions within tolerance. The IC-responsive fraction ranges from 38.5% to 56.8% (below 66.7 +/- 6.67 in every combination); the IRE-responsive fraction is within 77.8 +/- 7.78 only with both blocks under fig1e reading (a) (77.3% and 79.5%), where the IC fraction is 38.6% and 54.5%. Measured values are for fig1e reading (a), block ICwcfg1, test (a). The units are those of fig1e, which did not reproduce.

outcomes.statement: For IRE-responsive exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, the preferred orientation of the illusory bar matches that of the real bar in 78.6% of units.
outcomes.source: Figure 1g legend; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Comparison of the preferred orientation between illusory bars (I C stimuli) and real bars (I RE stimuli) for I RE -responsive and exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, showing a 78.6% match
outcomes.notes: The criterion judges the match under the reading that reproduces fig1f, and none does. The match ranges from 60.0% to 93.3%; only fig1e reading (a) with block ICwcfg1 gives a value within 78.6 +/- 7.86 (75.0%, 28 IRE-responsive units). Every reading is above its shuffle 95th percentile (37.1% to 67.9%).

outcomes.statement: Limiting the Neuropixels analysis to fixed-gaze trials (pupil within 8 degrees of its modal position) leaves 11 exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, and their responses to ICs and orientation match do not change the conclusion.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2b to 2e legends; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: When analyzing only fixed-gaze trials, there were n = 11 exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units; 10 sessions had eye tracking data and of these, 9 sessions had a valid receptive field mapping block where the fixed-gaze constraint left at least one trial in each position
outcomes.notes: Ten sessions have eye tracking, as in the paper. Under rule (r), any fixed-gaze RF trial counts for the coverage of the 9 positions, 9 sessions are valid, the paper's number; under rule (s), standard trials only, 8 are (session 630506 has no fixed-gaze standard trial at one position). Under rule (r) and fig1e reading (a), 10 exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units remain (within 11 +/- 1.1, in two sessions), and the orientation match (71.4% to 100% across tests and blocks, 7 to 9 IRE-responsive units) is above the shuffle 95th percentile (50.0% to 77.8%) in every combination. Under fig1e reading (b), 41 units remain. The units under rule (s) are the same 10, so the unit count rests on the session rule only through the session count. The fixed-gaze selection rests on the fig1e selection, which gives 44 units with all trials against the paper's 18, so the match of the fixed-gaze count may be partly coincidental.
deviations: The 8 degree threshold of the Methods cannot be applied, as the files give pupil position in camera pixels with no conversion; the code's 20 pixels (criterion reading b) is used.

Assumption. The criterion and the Extended Data Fig. 2 legend require that fixed-gaze RF trials cover all 9 positions ("at least one trial in each position") without saying whether inverse trials count. Rule (r), any RF trial, is adopted, as neither text restricts the trials to standard patches; it gives the paper's 9 sessions, where standard trials only give 8. A valid session with no fixed-gaze standard trial at a position gets p = 1 there. Asked of the authors under findings (methods_unavailable).
The shuffle 95th percentile of 1,000 permutations is the criterion's standard choice for the null of the match.

outcomes.statement: Receptive field positions mapped with fixed-gaze trials match those mapped with all trials for 81% of the 398 V1 RS units with significant receptive fields.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2f legend
outcomes.quote: Match proportion is 0.81 among 398 V1 RS units with significant receptive fields (p < 0.05 Kruskal-Wallis test across responses to 9 positions in the receptive field mapping block)
outcomes.notes: On the 8 sessions of rule (s), reading (b) gives n = 414 with a match of 0.812 and reading (c) n = 374 with 0.832; on the 9 sessions of rule (r) of ed2b, (b) gives n = 434 with 0.804 and (c) n = 392 with 0.821. All are within 0.81 +/- 0.081 and 398 +/- 39.8. Reading (a) gives n = 602 (rule s) or 640 (rule r), outside tolerance.

outcomes.statement: Pupil area during the presentation does not differ across the images of the IC block.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2g legend
outcomes.quote: Pupil area, z-scored across each recording session, during visual presentation of various images in the IC block (n = 10 sessions with eye tracking data; p = 0.7220 Friedman test)
outcomes.notes: Friedman test across the 10 sessions with eye tracking: p = 0.356 for IC1, LC1, LC2 and IC2 (reading a) and p = 0.898 for all 22 images (reading b), both >= 0.05 (paper p = 0.722). The range of image means is 0.011 and 0.045 s.d. The end and maximum variants give p from 0.063 to 0.948; trials whose eye frames are all NaN now give NaN for the maximum, not -inf.

outcomes.statement: Eye gaze is confined to a small region that fits within the illusory gap, with no systematic difference in pupil position among IC1, LC1, LC2 and IC2 presentations.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2a legend; Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Mouse eye gaze is confined to a small region that fits within the illusory gap region. There are no systematic differences in pupil position among I C1 vs. L C1 vs. L C2 vs. I C2 presentations
outcomes.notes: Friedman test of the per-session image means of the pupil center: p = 0.472 for x and 0.374 for y; the largest difference between image means in a session is 2.2 pixels. Per-session Kruskal-Wallis variant, p < 0.05 in 1 of 20 tests (smallest 0.026). Whether the gaze region fits within the illusory gap cannot be judged: the extent of the 0.01 density isoline is 24 to 124 camera pixels by session, and the files give no conversion to degrees.
deviations: The paper names no test for the absence of systematic differences; the criterion's Friedman test is a reader's choice.

outcomes.statement: V1 IC-encoders (n = 79) are more likely than V1 segment responders (n = 526) to receive putative excitatory connections from higher visual areas, by cross-correlogram analysis.
outcomes.source: Figure 2d legend; Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: V1 IC-encoders ( n = 79) are substantially more likely than V1 segment responders ( n = 526) to receive putative excitatory connections from higher visual areas (LM, RL, AL, PM and AM)

statistics.n: 79 V1 IC-encoders and 526 V1 segment responders, 12 sessions from 12 mice

outcomes.notes: The groups hold 79 V1 IC-encoders and 526 V1 segment responders, the paper's numbers. In all 8 combinations of smoothing (boxcar, Gaussian), flank (raw, corrected) and measure (fraction, number of connected HVA units), IC-encoders have the larger mean and P(IC-encoder > segment responder) from 0.62 to 0.64, with a tie-corrected two-sided rank-sum p from 1.0e-05 to 3.9e-04 (paper 7.0e-06). The medians are higher for IC-encoders in 7 combinations; for the number of connections with boxcar smoothing and the raw flank they are equal (1 and 1, p = 9.8e-05). The criterion requires a higher median and p < 0.05 under every combination; 7 of 8 meet it, so the readings differ and the criterion sends the claim to blocked (methods_underspecified). The effect the claim describes is present under every combination.
deviations: The per-pair normalisation by the square root of the spike counts is left out; it does not change the comparison of a pair's peak with its own flank.

outcomes.statement: A linear SVM decodes the four images IC1, LC1, LC2 and IC2 from V1 activity in the Neuropixels data with tenfold cross-validation accuracy above the chance of 0.25.
outcomes.source: Figure 3a; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The tenfold cross-validation performance was substantially above chance, indicating that neural activity patterns evoked by these four images were highly distinct at the multivariate level
outcomes.notes: V1 accuracy 0.697 +/- 0.052 under reading (a) and 0.719 +/- 0.056 under reading (b), against the chance of 0.25, signed-rank p = 0.00049 under both, 12 of 12 sessions above 0.25 (range 0.268 to 0.887 under reading a). The other areas range from 0.48 (AM) to 0.709 (LM) under reading (a).

outcomes.statement: In Neuropixels V1, TRE trials are decoded as the matching IC image more often than as the matching LC image (0.51 against 0.22), so IC inference is represented in V1.
outcomes.source: Figure 3c; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Applying inference decoding to Neuropixels V1 recordings revealed that T RE was substantially more likely to be decoded as I C than as L C (Fig. 3c ; decoding probability for I C vs. L C was 0.51 vs. 0.22, P < 0.05 Wilcoxon signed-rank test)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), P(TRE -> IC) = 0.518 and P(TRE -> LC) = 0.210, both within tolerance, IC above LC in 10 of 12 sessions, signed-rank p = 0.0024. Under reading (a), 0.516 and 0.197, the LC value 0.0014 below the lower bound 0.198, same p. With two further cross-validation seeds, both values are within tolerance under both readings, reading (a) IC 0.513 and 0.511, LC 0.198 and 0.199, p = 0.0024 (decoding_checks_shin_2025.ipynb), reading (b) IC 0.519 and 0.514, LC 0.209 and 0.215, p = 0.0015 and 0.0068 (decoding_seed1_shin_2025.ipynb, decoding_seed2_shin_2025.ipynb), so the outcome does not depend on the seed.
deviations: The decoder is scikit-learn's libsvm SVM, not MATLAB's fitcecoc; reading (b) searches C from 10^-3 to 1 with one-vs-one coding in place of the code's Bayesian search. On the first outer fold of the V1 sessions, C above 1 gave a lower best inner accuracy in all 12 (by 0.005 to 0.064), from fits that partly did not converge (12 to 17 of 36 per C value), and the one-vs-all coding changed the best inner accuracy by -0.012 to 0.024 (decoding_checks_shin_2025.ipynb).

outcomes.statement: In the Neuropixels data almost every visual area decodes TRE as IC more than as LC, significantly in V1, LM, RL, AL and PM and not in AM, with V1, LM and AL the strongest.
outcomes.source: Figure 3d legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: In the Neuropixels dataset, almost every visual area was substantially biased toward decoding T RE as I C than L C , with V1, LM and AL showing the strongest representations of the IC
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), adopted, the first seed gives four areas that decode TRE as IC significantly more than as LC (V1 p = 0.0024, LM 0.0156, RL 0.0049, AL 0.0020; PM 0.077, AM 0.083), with LM, V1 and AL the three largest mean scores (0.346, 0.308, 0.285). The two further seeds give five significant areas each, V1, LM, RL, AL and PM (PM p = 0.0425, AM p = 0.083) and V1, LM, RL, AL and AM (AM p = 0.0186, PM p = 0.052), with LM, V1 and AL the three largest. Under reading (a), five areas are significant with all three seeds (V1, LM, RL, AL and AM; PM p = 0.092 with the first seed) and V1, LM and AL are the three largest. The criterion is met in five of six runs. V1, LM, RL and AL are significant and LM, V1 and AL the three largest in all six; only the fifth area changes, and PM p runs from 0.0425 to 0.092 and AM p from 0.0020 to 0.083. The statement names PM as significant and AM as not; that set appears only with reading (b) and seed +100000, and the criterion counts areas without naming them. Sessions per area 12, 8, 11, 10, 12, 11, as in the paper.
deviations: Assumption. The Methods do not say how the SVM hyperparameters were set; the paper's code chooses them with OptimizeHyperparameters. Reading (b), C chosen by an inner cross-validation, is adopted as the reading closer to the code. It searches C from 10^-3 to 1 with one-vs-one coding. On the first outer fold of each session of V1, PM and AM, C above 1 gave a higher best inner accuracy in 1 of 35 sessions (PM, by 0.001), from fits that mostly did not converge (PM 28 to 30 and AM 30 of 33 or 36 per C value), and the one-vs-all coding changed the best inner accuracy by -0.026 to 0.027, which could change the chosen coding in some sessions; its effect on the inference scores was not computed (decoding_checks_shin_2025.ipynb). Asked of the authors under findings (methods_unavailable).

Assumption. The cross-validation partition is random, and reading (b) meets the criterion with two of three seeds (the first seed gives four significant areas). The outcome follows the majority of the seeds, a rule chosen after the first seed's result and not stated in the criterion. A rule requiring every seed would give partially reproduced; averaging the per-session scores over the seeds was not computed.
The decoder is scikit-learn's libsvm SVM, not MATLAB's fitcecoc.

outcomes.statement: Decoders trained on the XRE real-bar images classify IC1 and IC2 trials as the XRE image whose real bar matches the illusory bar, above chance in all six Neuropixels areas.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 7b legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 7
outcomes.quote: As with T RE inference decoding (Fig. 2 ), layer 2/3 of V1 and LM consistently show high inference scores (*p < 0.05, Wilcoxon signed-rank test compared to chance of 0.5
outcomes.notes: The XRE inference score is above 0.5 in all six areas under both readings, with signed-rank p from 0.0005 (V1) to 0.0137 (AM), equal or close to the paper's values (0.0005 to 0.0137). Mean scores 0.576 (AM) to 0.718 (V1) under reading (a) and 0.585 to 0.762 under reading (b); the chance of the two-class decoder is 0.5.

outcomes.statement: No higher visual area shows a substantially larger inference performance than V1, although decoding accuracy and inference scores differ across areas.
outcomes.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 9; Extended Data Fig. 7a and 7c legends
outcomes.quote: Notably, none of the higher visual areas showed a substantially larger inference performance compared to V1 (Extended Data Fig. 7a,c )

TRE inference score across the six areas, Neuropixels (Extended Data Fig. 7a)

outcomes.notes: No higher visual area has a significantly larger TRE or XRE inference score than V1 under either pairwise test (signed-rank, Tukey-Kramer) or either decoder reading; every significant difference has the HVA below V1. These are PM and AM in several measures, RL in XRE accuracy (both readings) and XRE score (reading b, signed-rank p = 0.0244 and Tukey-Kramer), and LM in XRE accuracy under reading (b) (signed-rank p = 0.0234). The Kruskal-Wallis tests across the six areas are significant, as in the paper: reading (a) p = 0.0006, 0.0071, 0.0005 and 0.0077 for accuracy, inference score, XRE accuracy and XRE score (paper 0.0019, 0.0249, 0.0005, 0.0022); reading (b) 0.0017, 0.0156, 0.0002 and 0.0015.
deviations: Extended Data Fig. 7c pools Neuropixels and 2p areas; its Kruskal-Wallis values are compared on the six Neuropixels areas only (criterion).

outcomes.statement: Decoders of other kinds (quadratic and radial basis function SVMs, a fully connected neural network) give results highly consistent with the linear SVM.
outcomes.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 8; Supplementary Fig. 3 (not read); Methods, Decoding analysis, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In addition, different types of decoders yielded highly consistent results (Supplementary Fig. 3 )
outcomes.notes: The quadratic and RBF SVMs were run (reading a, C = 1, one further seed): the TRE inference score is positive and significant in V1, LM and AL for both, as for the linear SVM on the same seed (p from 0.0015 to 0.0156 for the three kernels; mean scores 0.257 to 0.335). The network of the Methods (two hidden layers of 100 units, 50,000 full-batch epochs, tenfold) takes 4.38 ms per epoch on 89 units in this run, about 3.7 minutes per fit and about 18 hours on one core for the 300 fits of V1, LM and AL (the timing varies between runs; the run the verifier reviewed printed 3.60 ms and 15 hours), far beyond the notebook limit of 30 minutes. The criterion needs each decoder type, so the claim is not decided; the part that ran agrees with it.
deviations: The quadratic kernel is (gamma <x, y> + 1)^2 and the RBF kernel uses scikit-learn's gamma "scale"; the paper gives no kernel parameters (assumption, stated in the helper).
Supplementary Fig. 3 was not read; the test on the Neuropixels areas V1, LM and AL is the criterion's reading.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the 12 Neuropixels sessions only. The 2p imaging (V1L2/3, V1L4, mesoscope) and 2p holographic optogenetics recordings behind Figures 1h to 1k, 2b, 2c, 3e and 4 to 6 and several Extended Data figures are not in it, and the paper names no public archive for them; 21 of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

The units tables hold units whose quality is labelled noise (539 of 3,026 units in sub-633229, 322 of the V1 units across sessions), while the Methods state that all units not classified as noise were packaged into the NWB files.
The Methods' Animals list 14 Neuropixels mice (Sst-IRES-Cre;Ai32 n = 10, PV-IRES-Cre;Ai32 n = 4); the files hold 12 sessions from 12 mice (9 Sst, 3 Pvalb), as the Results and legends state.

The eye tracking pupil position (pupil_tracking/data) is stated in meters; its values (pupil center near 300 to 400, pupil half-width near 20) are camera pixels, and no conversion to visual degrees is given, so the Methods' 8 degree fixed-gaze criterion cannot be applied from the files.
The Methods say eye video was acquired at 30 Hz; the eye tracking timestamps in the files are 16.7 ms apart (60 Hz), which is what the paper's code assumes.

The IC block tables give each image only as a frame index (0 to 21) with no image names; the names come from the paper's code, and the image templates stored in the files allow them to be checked by eye.
The last eye tracking timestamp of each session with eye tracking is NaN.

For the authors. The Methods do not say how the SVM hyperparameters were set; the code calls fitcecoc with OptimizeHyperparameters auto. Which coding, box constraint and kernel scale were chosen per session and area? The significance of PM and AM in Fig. 3d depends on it here (four areas significant with C chosen by inner cross-validation, five with C = 1), and with C chosen by inner cross-validation it also depends on the cross-validation partition (five areas with each of two further seeds, PM significant with one and AM with the other).

For the authors. Extended Data Fig. 2 counts sessions whose fixed-gaze RF trials left at least one trial in each position. Do inverse-patch trials count towards that coverage? Counting them gives the paper's 9 sessions; counting standard trials only gives 8.

For the authors. Extended Data Fig. 6b counts 87 V1 IC-encoders and 636 segment responders. Are these all units in the NWB files, including those whose quality column says noise? All units give exactly 87 and 636; dropping the units labelled noise gives 79 and 566.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The record then had all 18 Neuropixels claims and supp3 blocked (too_large) because the author's run ended before the notebook was executed. The verifier gave its own outcome for each claim from the outputs; agreement is against that record, so it disagrees on every tested Neuropixels claim. It queried the DANDI API for the blocked 2p claims and tested the helpers on synthetic inputs.

disagreements.reason: V1 has 150.3 +/- 19.8 RS units per session (1,804 in total); higher visual areas have 582.8 +/- 43.3, within 597 +/- 46.
159 units are IC-encoders in at least one block (reading a), exactly the paper's 159; reading b gives 163.

Reading b1 (all V1 units in the files, ICwcfg1) gives exactly 87 IC-encoders and 636 segment responders. Dropping units labelled noise gives 79 and 566 (problem 6). The literal filter (b2) would fail the claim; the exact 87 and 636 under b1 strongly support the notebook's reading.
All six areas hold IC-encoders: between 48 and 79 per area, and in 8 to 12 sessions per area.

44 exclusively center-responsive units under reading a and 52 under reading b, against 18 +/- 1.8. The V1 RS count of 1,804 matches. It asked for a count of fig1e units before the exclusivity step, to locate where 44 or 52 diverge from 18.

No combination puts both fractions within tolerance. IC-responsive ranges from 38.5% to 56.8% against 66.7 +/- 6.67; IRE-responsive is within tolerance only under block (ii) (77.3% and 79.5%). This rests on the unit set of fig1e, which did not reproduce.

The criterion ties the result to a reading that reproduces fig1f, and none does. The match ranges from 60.0% to 93.3%; only fig1e (a), block (i) gives 75.0%, within 78.6 +/- 7.86. Every reading is above its shuffle 95th percentile.

10 sessions have eye tracking. Only 8 sessions are valid, against the paper's 9, and the criterion requires an exact match. Under fig1e reading a, 10 units remain (within 11 +/- 1.1) and the match is above the shuffle 95th percentile. A session counts as valid only if its fixed-gaze standard RF trials cover all 9 positions, while the legend says "at least one trial in each position"; session 630506 covers 8 positions with standard trials only, and counting inverse trials was not tried (problem 4).
Reading b gives n = 414 with a match of 0.812; reading c gives n = 374 with 0.832. Both are within 398 +/- 39.8 and 0.81 +/- 0.081.
Friedman p = 0.356 for reading a and 0.898 for reading b, both >= 0.05. For trials whose eye frames are all NaN, the area_max variant becomes -inf, so its range prints as NaN or inf (problem 9).
Friedman p = 0.47 for x and 0.37 for y. The confinement extent is reported only in camera pixels (24 to 124 px), so "fits within the gap" cannot be judged.

Group sizes are exactly 79 and 526, and all 8 combinations give IC-encoders the higher mean with rank-sum p <= 5e-4. But under boxcar, raw flank, number of connections, the medians tie at 1 and 1. The criterion requires a higher median under every combination, otherwise blocked (methods_underspecified). The rule is brittle on a tie of integer medians (problem 5); stats.ranksums has no tie correction (problem 10).
V1 accuracy is 0.697 (decoder reading a) and 0.719 (reading b), with signed-rank p = 0.00049 against the chance of 0.25 under both.

Under decoder reading b, TRE is decoded as IC 0.518 and as LC 0.210, both within tolerance, with p = 0.0024. Under reading a, LC is 0.1966, just below the tolerance bound of 0.198. The grid search of reading b covers only C from 1e-3 to 1 and its fits hit max_iter; with a single cross-validation seed the outcome is fragile (problem 3).

Reproduced per the criterion: five areas are significant and the three largest mean scores are V1, LM and AL. But the significant set is V1, LM, RL, AL and AM; PM is not (p = 0.092), while AM is (p = 0.0029), the reverse of the paper. Decoder reading a only; reading b could change it (problem 2). The criterion counts significant areas without naming them (problem 8).
All 6 areas are above 0.5, with p from 0.0005 to 0.0137, close to the paper's values. The chance level of 0.5 matches.
Under both readings, every significant V1-versus-HVA difference has the HVA lower. Kruskal-Wallis p-values are 0.0006, 0.0071, 0.0005 and 0.0077, all significant like the paper's.
No area gives p < 0.05 in either panel. Eleven of the 12 p-values equal the paper's to 4 decimals.

With boxcar smoothing, raw flank and number of connections, the medians are 1 and 1, so that combination fails the rule. The direction of the rank-sum test is not a median comparison. The protocol rule cited for the tie-break was not available to the verifier. The substance supports the claim (P = 0.63, p = 9.8e-05, 68% against 50% of units with any connection). The outcome rests on that tie-break, but the record does not mark it assumed; it is only listed as a deviation. Still judged blocked (methods_underspecified).

entries.name: 000248-shin-2025
entries.title: Illusory contour responses in mouse visual cortex, Neuropixels (Shin et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the Neuropixels findings of Shin, Ogando, Abdeladim and colleagues (2025) on dandiset 000248, which holds 12 Neuropixels sessions with six probes in V1, LM, RL, AL, PM and AM while mice viewed illusory contour images. It counts the units and the IC-encoders and segment responders, selects exclusively center-responsive V1 units, repeats the analyses on fixed-gaze trials, computes cross-correlograms between V1 and higher visual areas, and decodes the images and the inference of the illusory contour from each area. The 2p imaging and holography data of the paper are not in the dandiset.
